Verify Simplicial Complex Against igraph

Source: R/simplicial.R
verify_simplicial.Rd

verify_simplicial() builds the clique complex of mat with build_simplicial() and checks it against two independent references: its simplices against the cliques igraph::cliques() finds in the same thresholded graph, and its Euler characteristic against the alternating sum of its Betti numbers (the Euler-Poincare theorem). It prints the result of each check and the Betti numbers, and is meant for testing. It needs igraph, and raises an error without it.

Usage

verify_simplicial(mat, threshold = 0)

Arguments

mat

A square weight matrix, or a network object whose weight matrix build_simplicial() reads (a netobject, tna model, cograph_network or net_hon).

threshold

The smallest absolute edge weight an edge needs to enter, as in build_simplicial(). Default 0.

Value

A list, invisibly: cliques_match (whether the simplices equal the cliques from igraph::cliques() exactly), n_simplices_ours, n_simplices_igraph, betti, euler and f_vector. The two checks are printed as a side effect.

Details

The complex is built with the default max_dim = 10, while igraph::cliques() has no size limit, so a graph with a clique of more than 11 nodes reports a mismatch, with a warning of class nestimate_truncated_complex from betti_numbers().

Examples

mat <- matrix(c(0,.6,.5,.6,0,.4,.5,.4,0), 3, 3)
colnames(mat) <- rownames(mat) <- c("A","B","C")
verify_simplicial(mat, threshold = 0.3)
#>   Cliques:  MATCH (7 simplices)
#>   Betti:    b0=1 b1=0 b2=0
#>   Euler:    1 (Euler-Poincare: VERIFIED)
